sources.title: Sancerre (wine) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Sancerre is highly regarded for white wine made from the Sauvignon blanc grape. However both Sancerre rouge and Sancerre rosé are made, representing approximately 20% and less than 1%, respectively, of Sancerre's total output. The basis for both the red and rosé is, as in nearby Burgundy and Champagne, the red grape Pinot noir.

sources.title: Sancerre (wine) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Most – but not all – of the Sauvignon blancs are unoaked. ... Around the village of Chavignol (considered a cru of Sancerre), the soil also includes some Kimmeridgian marl. sources.title: Pouilly-Fumé - Wikipedia
sources.quote: "Fumé" also refers to the smoky bouquet (the renowned "gun flint aroma"), bestowed by the terroir vineyards of Pouilly-sur-Loire. ... This varietal Sauvignon is similar to those of the vineyards of Sancerre.

sources.quote: The northern sub-region produces red wines from the Syrah grape, sometimes blended with up to 20% of white wine grapes, and white wines from Marsanne, Roussanne and Viognier grapes. The southern sub-region produces an array of red, white and rosé wines, often blends of several grapes such as in Châteauneuf-du-Pape.

Mukuzani has a deep red color with a soft smoky scent of oak and berry.

sources.title: Barbera d'Asti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Under the DOCG rules, a minimum of 90% Barbera grapes must be used; the balance may be made up with either Freisa, Grignolino or Dolcetto grapes. The wine must be made before the date of 1 March immediately following the harvest, and must reach a minimum alcohol content of 11.5% ABV.

sources.title: Barbera d'Asti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Barbera d'Asti Superiore must have an alcoholic strength of at least 12.5% by volume, and be aged for at least 14 months, 6 months of which stored in oak or chestnut barrels. Many superiore producers refine it in small oak barriques to obtain a rounder taste. The superiore has the following sub-zones indicated on the label: Nizza, Tinella, or Colli Astiani (Asti). The superiore wine has a strong additional aging potential; it can often be aged from ten to twenty years.

sources.title: Nizza DOCG - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Nizza (also Barbera d'Asti Superiore Nizza before 2014) is a DOCG red Italian wine produced in the northern Italian region of Piedmont. ... Grape composition: 100% Barbera ... Minimum alcohol: 13% (13.5% if a single vineyard is named on the label)

sources.title: Barbera d'Asti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The Nizza production rules require the use of 100% Barbera grapes, a maximum yield of 7 tonnes per hectare, and minimum aging of 18 months, of which 6 months must be in oak barrels.

sources.title: Barbaresco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Barbaresco is an Italian wine made from the Nebbiolo grape. Barbaresco is produced in the Piedmont region in an area of the Langhe immediately to the east of Alba and specifically in the comunes of Barbaresco, Treiso and Neive

sources.title: Barbaresco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: It was granted Denominazione di origine controllata (DOC) status in 1966 and Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita (DOCG) status in 1980. The wine is often compared with Barolo—another Nebbiolo-based wine from the Piedmont area.

sources.title: Barbaresco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Located east of Barbaresco and the largest of the villages, Neive is responsible for 31 per cent of Barbaresco's production and makes some of the most full-bodied and tannic examples of the wine.

sources.title: Barbaresco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The area is also home to the highly esteemed Nebbiolo vineyards of Santo Stefano in the cru of Albesani, with its ideal south-western exposure in the centre of the Albesani hill, and Bricco di Neive, whose names are starting to appear on some single-vineyard bottlings.

sources.title: Barbaresco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: DOCG regulations stipulate that Barbaresco wines must be aged for a minimum of 2 years (at least 9 months in wooden barrels) prior to release and for at least 4 years to be considered a riserva. The wines must have a minimum alcohol level of 12.5 per cent, though most are closer to 13.5 per cent.

sources.title: Barolo - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Barolo ... is a red denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG) wine produced in the northern Italian region of Piedmont. It is made from the nebbiolo grape and is often described as one of Italy's greatest wines.

sources.title: Barolo - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In addition to restrictions on yield and alcohol levels, to be labelled DOCG, a Barolo must be aged at least three years (a minimum of 38 months from November 1 the year of harvest), of which a minimum 18 months in wooden barrels. For wines labelled Barolo Riserva, five years of total ageing is required (a minimum of 62 months from November 1 the year of harvest), again with a minimum of 18 months in barrel.

sources.title: Barolo - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The zone of production extends into the communes of Barolo, Castiglione Falletto, Serralunga d'Alba and parts of the communes of Cherasco, Diano d'Alba, Grinzane Cavour, La Morra, Monforte d'Alba, Novello, Roddi, and Verduno, all in the province of Cuneo, south-west of Alba.

sources.title: Barolo - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Planted with soils higher in sand, limestone, iron, phosphorus and potassium, the wines of Serralunga Valley tend to be austere and powerful and require significant ageing (at least 12–15 years) to develop. ... These wines tend to be less tannic and full-bodied than those from the Serralunga Valley and can require less ageing (8 to 10 years).

sources.title: Barolo - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The Barolo zone is located 3 km (1.9 mi) southwest of the Barbaresco zone with only the vineyards of Diano d'Alba planted with Dolcetto between the two nebbiolo strongholds.

sources.title: 바롤로 - 위키백과
sources.quote: 바롤로는 타르와 장미의 아로마를 갖는 것으로 설명되며 포도주들은 숙성이 가능하기에 숙성될수록 녹슨 붉은 빛깔을 내는 것이 보통이다. 바롤로는 출시 전 수확 이후 적어도 36개월은 숙성해야 하며, 그 중 최소 18개월은 나무 안에 있어야 한다. 출시 전 최소 5년 숙성되면 포도주의 레이블에 Riserva를 붙일 수 있다.

sources.quote: Wines made from Primitivo have notes of plum and spice, like Zinfandel, but because of different growing soils and climate, the fruit character is less jammy, the structure more akin to old world wines, with rustic notes of earth and spice, as well as tamed fruit flavors.

sources.title: Tuscan wine - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Super Tuscans are an unofficial category of Tuscan wines, not recognized within the Italian wine classification system.

sources.title: Tuscan wine - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Most producers have brought their Super Tuscans back under legal regulations, notably since the creation of the less restrictive IGT Toscana designation in 1992 and the DOC Bolgheri designation in 1994, while the pioneer Sassicaia was prized with its own exclusive Bolgheri Sassicaia DOC.

sources.title: Tuscan wine - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In addition to wines based on the Sangiovese grape, many well known Super Tuscans are based on a "Bordeaux-blend", meaning a combination of grapes typical for Bordeaux (especially Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot).

sources.title: Carmignano DOCG - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Current DOCG regulations mandate that Sangiovese must constitute at least 50% of the blend, allowing up to 10–20% Cabernet Sauvignon or Cabernet Franc

sources.title: Morellino di Scansano - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Morellino is the local name for the Sangiovese grape variety. The wine, which was granted DOC status in 1978, then upgraded to DOCG status beginning with the 2007 vintage, is made from at least 85% Sangiovese

cherry.title: Wine Folly - Guide to Sangiovese Wine

sources.title: Bolgheri - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Due to the particular characteristics of the soil and micro climate sunny, dry and moderately windy, the grape varieties of Bordeaux origin tend to thrive, such as Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. ... Among the most known "Super Tuscan" producers are Tenuta San Guido who produce Sassicaia, Tenuta Dell'Ornellaia who produce Ornellaia

sources.title: Bolgheri - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The current set of DOC regulations for Bolgheri red wines became approved in 1994. Before the creation of this DOC, the "Super Tuscans" from the area were typically sold under the simpler designations Vino da tavola or IGT Toscana. The appellation rules determine that in Bolgheri Rosso and Bolgheri Rosé, Sangiovese may be utilised only to a degree of 70%, and in excess of this a wine must be classified IGT. Cabernet Sauvignon from 10 to 80%, Merlot, up to 80% and other local red varieties, up to 30%. Rosso must be aged for 24 months.

sources.title: Bolgheri - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The sub-zone Sassicaia has its own appellation declaration, with up to 85% of Cabernet Sauvignon and 15% Cabernet Franc. Bolgheri Sassicaia must be aged for 26 months.

sources.title: Bolgheri - Wikipedia
sources.quote: For Bolgheri Bianco, Tuscan Trebbiano from 10 to 70%, Vermentino from 10 to 70%, Sauvignon blanc from 10 to 70% and other local white varieties, up to 30%. Two varietal wines are permitted, Sauvignon blanc and Vermentino

sources.title: Chianti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Only Chianti from this sub-zone may display the black rooster (gallo nero) seal on the neck of the bottle, which indicates that the producer of the wine is a member of the Chianti Classico Consortium, the local association of producers.

sources.title: Chianti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Chianti Classico must have a minimum alcohol level of 12% with a minimum of 7 months aging in oak, while Chianti Classicos labeled riserva must be aged at least 24 months at the winery, with a minimum alcohol level of 12.5%. ... For basic Chianti, the minimum alcohol level is 11.5%

sources.title: Chianti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Chianti that meets more stringent requirements (lower yield, higher alcohol content and dry extract) may be labelled as Chianti Superiore, although Chianti from the Classico sub-area is not allowed in any event to be labelled as Superiore.

sources.title: Chianti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In 2014, a new category of Chianti Classico was introduced: Chianti Classico Gran Selezione. Gran Selezione is made exclusively from a winery's own grapes grown according to stricter regulations compared to regular Chianti Classico.

sources.title: Chianti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The sub-zones are (clockwise from the north): the Colli Fiorentini which is located south of the city of Florence; Chianti Rufina in the northeastern part of the zone located around the commune of Rufina; Classico in the centre of Chianti, across the provinces of Florence and Siena; Colli Aretini in the Arezzo province to the east; Colli Senesi south of Chianti Classico in the Siena hills, ... Colline Pisane, the westernmost sub-zone in the province of Pisa; Montespertoli located within the Colli Fiorentini around the commune of Montespertoli; Montalbano in the north-west part of the zone

sources.title: Chianti - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Chianti Classico are premium Chianti wines that tend to be medium-bodied with firm tannins and medium-high to high acidity.

sources.title: Brunello di Montalcino - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Brunello di Montalcino is a red DOCG Italian wine produced in the vineyards surrounding the town of Montalcino ... Brunello di Montalcino is made 100% from Sangiovese.

sources.title: Brunello di Montalcino - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Most producers will separate their production between a Normale and Riserva bottling. The Normale bottles are released on the market 50 months after harvest and the Riserva are released a year afterward.

sources.title: Brunello di Montalcino - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Rosso di Montalcino is made from 100% Sangiovese grown in the same delineated region as Brunello di Montalcino. ... Rosso di Montalcino is typically lighter, fresher and more approachable upon release

sources.title: Brunello di Montalcino - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In 1996, Italian authorities approved the Sant'Antimo DOC to allow Montalcino producers to produce DOC designated wines that were not 100% Sangiovese.

sources.title: Prosecco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Within the larger designation are two small DOCG areas, Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco in the hills between the comuni (municipalities) of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene, and Asolo Prosecco around the nearby comune of Asolo. Prosecco Superiore is always spumante and comes only from these DOCG areas.

sources.title: Prosecco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Depending on their sweetness, in accordance with the EU Sweetness of wine Regulations for Terms used to indicate sweetness of sparkling wine, Proseccos are labelled "Brut" (up to 12 grams per litre of residual sugar), "Extra Dry" (12–17 g/L) or "Dry" (17–32 g/L). Extra-Dry has been the dominant style made, but the amount of Brut is now increasing.

sources.title: Prosecco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Prosecco has a minimum of 10.5–11.5% alcohol by volume, depending on the DOC/DOCG rules.

sources.title: Prosecco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Most Prosecco, whether DOC or DOCG, is made as Spumante sparkling wine or Frizzante (semi-sparkling). Prosecco DOC Spumante is the most famous and popular variety, with longer-lasting bubbles. Prosecco DOC Frizzante has bubbles that linger for a shorter time.

sources.title: Prosecco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Glera grapes made in a Prosecco style outside the DOC/DOCG have a non-protected designation, such as "IGT Veneto", are generally cheaper and of more variable quality and cannot be called Prosecco.

sources.title: Prosecco - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Since 2020, the DOC rules allow a rosé variety of Prosecco designated spumante rosé, which must contain Glera blended with 10–15% Pinot nero.

sources.title: Soave (wine) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Within the Soave region are both a denominazione di origine controllata (DOC) zone and, since 2001, a denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG) designation known as Soave Superiore, with both zones being further sub-divided into a general and Classico designation for the wines produced in the heartland of the Soave region

sources.title: Soave (wine) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Only white wine is produced in the Soave region, and a minimum of 70% must be the Garganega grape. ... All the grapes used for the DOC wine must be harvested to a yield no greater than 14 tonnes/hectare with the finished wine fermented to a minimum alcohol level of at least 10.5%.

sources.title: Soave (wine) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Grapes are harvested to a more restricted maximum yield of 10 tonnes/ha, while the finished DOCG wines must reach a minimum alcohol level of 11.5%.

sources.title: Soave (wine) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Today, the use of the specification "Classico" with the designation "Soave" is reserved for the product made from grapes harvested from the hillside vineyards around the municipalities of Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone, in the original and oldest classic "zone" of Verona.

sources.title: Soave (wine) - Wikipedia
sources.quote: While most Soave is dry, still wine, within the DOC zone a sparkling spumante style is permitted, as is the passito Recioto style, that in 1998 was granted its own DOCG designation for grapes grown in the hilly region.

sources.title: Valpolicella - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The red wine known as Valpolicella is typically made from three grape varieties: Corvina Veronese, Rondinella, and Molinara. A variety of wine styles are produced in the area, including a recioto dessert wine and Amarone, a strong wine made from dried grapes.

sources.title: Valpolicella - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Valpolicella Classico is made from grapes grown in the original Valpolicella production zone. Valpolicella Superiore is aged at least one year and has an alcohol content of at least 12 percent. Valpolicella Ripasso is a form of Valpolicella Superiore made with partially dried grape skins that have been left over from fermentation of Amarone or recioto.

sources.title: Valpolicella - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In December 2009, the production of Amarone and recioto dessert wines within the Valpolicella DOC received their own separate denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG) status.

sources.title: Amarone - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Amarone della Valpolicella, usually known as Amarone ... is an Italian DOCG denomination of typically rich dry red wine made from the partially dried grapes of the Corvina (45–95%, of which up to 50% could be substituted with Corvinone), Rondinella (5–30%) and other approved red grape varieties (up to 25%).

sources.title: Amarone - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The resulting wine is more tannic, with a deeper color, and having more alcohol and more extract. Alcohol content easily surpasses 15% (the legal minimum is 14%) and the resulting wine is rarely released until five years after the vintage, even though this is not a legal requirement.

sources.title: Amarone - Wikipedia
sources.quote: If fermentation is stopped early, the resulting wine will contain residual sugar (more than 4 grams of sugar per litre) and produce a sweeter wine known as Recioto della Valpolicella.

sources.title: Valpolicella - Wikipedia

sources.title: New Zealand wine - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Waipara, in Canterbury, represents another soil type. Viticulturists have planted Pinot Noir here because of the French experience of the affinity between the grape type and the chalky soil on the Côte-d'Or.

sources.title: Waipara - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The Waipara region has a reputation as a premium area for the production of Pinot noir, Riesling and Chardonnay.

sources.quote: Like many other New World wines, New Zealand wine is usually produced and labelled as single varietal wines, or if blended, winemakers list the varietal components on the label. ... New Zealand pioneered the use of screwtop closures in fine wines

sources.title: Central Otago wine region - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The Central Otago wine region is a geographical indication in New Zealand's South Island, and the world's southernmost commercial wine growing region. ... Pinot noir is the leading grape variety in Central Otago, estimated to account for over 80% of plantings. Sparkling wine is made in the traditional style from Pinot noir and Chardonnay grapes.

sources.title: Central Otago wine region - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Bannockburn is a small Geographical Indication on the southern banks of the Kawarau River near Cromwell and is a very warm area ... Gibbston is a tight valley enclosed by mountainous terrain. ... Gibbston is the coolest and highest of the sub-regions with vineyards between 320 and 420 metres (1,050 and 1,380 ft) altitude.

sources.title: Central Otago wine region - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The Alexandra Basin is surrounded by the Clutha River / Mata-Au and Manuherikia River and regularly records New Zealand's hottest summer temperatures. ... The Cromwell Basin contains the highest concentration of vines

sources.title: Marlborough wine region - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Although the Marlborough GI extends to the entire Marlborough and Kaikoura district boundaries, vineyards are broadly concentrated into three sub-regions. ... The Wairau Valley is the flood plain and valley floor of the Wairau River, around the town of Blenheim ... The Southern Valleys are the north–south tributary valleys on the southern slope of the Wairau Valley. ... Awatere Valley is further to the south-east and south of the Wither Hills.

sources.title: New Zealand wine - Wikipedia
sources.quote: New Zealand pioneered the use of screwtop closures in fine wines because of the frequency of quality issues affecting wines being shipped long distances with cork closures.

sources.title: New Zealand wine - Wikipedia
sources.quote: For example, it is common to see an Auckland producer market a "Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc" or a Marlborough producer market a "Gisborne Chardonnay".

sources.quote: Ruby Ports are younger, being aged only a few years or less - they include regular Ruby Ports (often called "Fine Ruby"), Ruby Reserve Ports, Late Bottled Vintage Ports, Crusted Ports, and Vintage Ports. Tawny Ports are aged in barrel for typically much longer before release and, with the exception of the least-aged tawny Ports, have an indication of age in 10 year increments between 10 to 50 years. Colheitas are also a type of tawny Port, which are a barrel-aged Port made from grapes of a single year's harvest.
